newsitem.title: CANADA: BHP reaches pact with Canada native group.
newsitem.headline: BHP reaches pact with Canada native group.

text.p: Broken Hill Proprietary Co Ltd said Wednesday it reached an agreement on sharing of economic benefits with one of the four native groups near the site of its proposed diamond mine in Canada's Northwest Territories.

Jim Excell, the BHP manager of the Lac de Gras mine project, said an accord had been concluded with the so-called Treaty 11 Dogrib people subject to ratification by the group's members. He declined to give details of the agreement.
Dia Met Minerals Ltd is a partner in the mine project.
The company also hopes to soon conclude agreements with the other three groups -- the Inuit, Metis and so-called Treaty 8 Dogrib people.

In granting approval in principle for the mine in August, Canada's federal government said it wanted to see "substantial progress" toward the economic agreements before it gave final approval. It also called for substantial progress on an environmental protection and monitoring accord.
The government then said it aimed to make a decision on final approval this week but has not made any announcement.
Excell said the company believes it is "getting close" to fulfilling the government's demand for substantial progress.
The company wants swift approval so it can stick to a tight construction schedule that would allow it to begin diamond production in the second half of 1998.
The economic agreements were intended to provide such things as job guarantees for native people, training programs and other benefits for nearby communities.
